# Unify Dock and Neural Link undo on the group cursor

> **Reopened 2026-09-22 for original AC-2.** The merged Group source and agent/human cursor work remains delivered. The open boundary is deployed Neural Link undo/redo/list/save/replay with a real `groupId`; direct-service tests and one agent-write arm do not exercise that transport. [Closeout evidence](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18303#issuecomment-5785067897).

## Context

The Engine already exposes Neural Link begin/commit/undo/redo through a private `TransactionService` keyed by writer/session, while ordinary dock UI gestures bypass it. `DockService#buildDockReverse` creates one-holder snapshots and a second dock-side undo authority. D#18224 resolved that these must be migrated, not supplemented.

## The Problem

Two histories over one heap disagree under interleaving: writer A can undo an older whole-document snapshot over a newer human B mutation. A Group cursor must reverse B before A regardless of origin. Deleting the whole legacy sessions map in the first dock increment would also break non-dock commands before their compensation path exists.

## The Architectural Reality

All dock origins—human gesture, Workstation action, Neural Link dock operation, restore—target one Group. Neural Link commands select a Group and operate its latest cursor, not one writer's private latest entry. Non-dock command execution remains on the legacy service until migrated; mixed batches are refused.

## The Fix

Route dock begin/commit/undo/redo/list/save/replay into `manager.Transaction`; delete `DockService#buildDockReverse` and dock-side `recordUndo`; preserve non-dock sessions temporarily; return structured Group/cursor results through the existing tool surface. The delivered cut must be net-negative across replaced undo code.

## Ordinary popup admission

The all-dock-origin cut includes ordinary tear-out birth: admit a full Workspace and its semantic document through the Group claim before the first committed pop-out, then record that transition through the same Group history. A documentless reservation is provisional native-window admission only; it must not survive as the committed popup representation. Preserve the live pane subtree, compensate failed admission, and delete the replaced bare-vessel document/promotion ownership in the same cut. Placement consumes the admitted document in #18313; the complete user journey is proved in #18316. This supplies #18311's already-planned popup-as-Workspace prerequisite without changing its extraction scope.

## Accepted Group lifecycle boundary

Per D#18150 [step 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18289325) and its [terminal mapping](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18293826), this leaf accepts admissions, connection cache, vessel ownership and retirement directly into the settled Group. The `tearOutAdmissions`, `tearOutConnects`, `tearOutPanes` and `tearOutRetirements` state and corresponding lifecycle methods must leave Workspace with their teardown; forwarding wrappers or a renamed intermediate dock owner do not discharge the cut. #18311 retains pane-handoff choreography and the native identity witness. Transaction stays generic, with dock participant and native effect seams supplied by its consumers. Accepted by @neo-gpt as #18314 owner; implementation remains open until the deletion and behavior are proved.

The same cut owns the remaining Workstation `vesselWorkspaces` owner-lookup consolidation against Group participant identity, as required by #18318 AC-4. Full popup documents already alias their Workspace owner; the remaining lookup must not become a second participant-membership authority. Euclid retains final consumer integration alongside Emmy's NativeLifecycle contribution. This is accepted work, not a completed acceptance claim.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns criterion 7 and criterion 3's deletion ledger for the undo surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every dock-origin transaction enters the Group history; ordinary human gestures no longer bypass recording.
- [ ] Neural Link dock undo/redo/list/save/replay resolve a Group and operate its shared cursor.
- [ ] Agent A dock, human B mutation, undo twice reverses B then A through exactly one authoritative history.
- [ ] `DockService#buildDockReverse` and dock-side `recordUndo` are deleted with no parallel compatibility path.
- [ ] Non-dock command execution remains functional on the legacy service until its own migration; mixed dock/non-dock batches refuse before any partial replay.
- [ ] Structured refusals propagate without being treated as successful effects.
- [ ] The PR records a net-negative source deletion ledger for the replaced dock undo paths.

## Out of Scope

Migrating every non-dock command, Workstation button styling, or cross-Group undo.

## Avoided Traps

No second adapter history; no writer-private cursor; no wholesale sessions-map deletion; no partial mixed replay; no close-target overclaim for non-dock migration.

unit 3412/3412.

* docs(dock): state the Workspace facade contract instead of leaving each extraction to infer it (#18318)

An inferred facade becomes a forwarding shell one method at a time: every
extraction guesses which callbacks the host still owes its collaborators, and the
guesses do not have to agree. This states the contract so the next cut is measured
against a written thing.

Three parts, each written because it was actually costing something:

**The participant seam, as the four callbacks a host registers at bind time** —
`getDocument`, `setDocument`, optional `getRevision`, and `project`. The two
non-obvious clauses are the ones a participant can break silently: registration
never READS the document (the first transaction establishes the reference, so
binding cannot mint a phantom revision), and `project` must return the projection
promise and must NOT admit another write. That second one is the sole-mutation-path
invariant restated at the seam where a participant could otherwise violate it.

**The import direction, both ways, with the price tag on the half nobody guards.**
"The manager must not import the dock" keeps the manager general. The reverse
matters more concretely: this module lands in every single-window application, so
one static import of the topology manager pulls the whole multi-window machinery
into a download that never opens a second window. The manager IS reachable here
through a DYNAMIC import — that lazy edge is the boundary, not an oversight, and
the arm added earlier walks the static closure in both directions precisely so a
grep for the module name cannot report the intended edge as a violation.

**What this class still holds and should not.** Admissions, the connect cache,
committed vessel ownership and retained retirements are per-topology state living
in a per-workspace class. Naming them in the contract is the point: their owner is
the settled topology Group, they do not move into the gesture machine on the way,
and a reader who inherits this file should inherit the obligation rather than the
appearance of a finished facade.

Documentation only. Code lines flat at 1294; static closure 79 modules, 1493 ->
1495 KiB (docblock bytes, module count unchanged). unit 3412/3412.

The integration lane is removing the decode half: ownership will be recovered by

Verified on the contribution branch — the base class has zero references to the
decoder there, while the minting half remains.

That successor is strictly better, and it retires this guard by design. The hazard
these arms pin exists only because ownership is recovered by DECODING a key; a key
that is never parsed cannot be parsed inconsistently, so once the inverse is gone
there is nothing left to fall out of step.

So the block now carries its own retirement trigger, stated as an instruction to
DELETE rather than adapt — and explicitly against the failure mode where someone
preserves an unused inverse on the base class purely to keep these arms green. A
test that outlives its contract does not become harmless; it becomes a reason to
keep dead code.

The guard stays for now because the pair still exists on this base and the
half-override hazard is real until it does not.

unit 3419/3419.

* fix(dock): the facade contract states BOTH protocol layers, and the manager rule guards a domain (#18318)

Three bounded corrections from cross-family review. All three were right.

**RA-1 — two real contracts, and I had dismissed one as aspirational.** The
ticket's capture/prepare/adopt/project naming is not aspirational wording for the
adapter; it names the GENERIC participant protocol the transaction manager
executes, and that protocol is enforced rather than documented — a participant
missing any of `capture`/`prepare`/`adopt`/`compensate` has its transaction
refused. Its shape carries the atomicity guarantees: `capture` is synchronous and
must return value/generation/revision or it throws, `prepare` is the only phase
that may await, and `adopt`/`compensate` are synchronous BY REQUIREMENT because a
compensation that could await is a window in which a half-adopted topology is
observable. The docblock now states that layer alongside the adapter callbacks
`window/WorkspaceSet` composes out of it, and says why the distinction is
load-bearing: a host reading the adapter list alone would believe adoption may
await.

Also corrected: `project` receives the transaction CONTEXT, not a document. The
committed value is read from `context.snapshot`, and the adapter adds
`preserveItemIds` naming panes owned by sibling participants.

**RA-2 — my manager rule exempted the dock module most likely to be imported.**
Direction B named `Workspace` and `WorkspaceDocument`, so every other dock module
was exempt by omission — and transitive walking cannot rescue that for
`window/TearOut.mjs`, whose entire static closure is itself (measured: 1 module).
The old predicate caught 0 of it; the rule is now the dock DIRECTORY, and an
import-free crossing control pins exactly that case.

Worse, my own innocent-neighbour control listed `dock/window/TearOut.mjs` —
asserting a dock module was innocent under the manager rule, encoding the very
exemption the rule exists to forbid, inside the control meant to police it. The
neighbours are now non-dock modules.

**RA-3 — do not land a guard for a decoder that is already being removed.** The
integration branch resolves ownership by matching the exact reserved workspace key
and has deleted the base decoder. Leaving a new test plus a comment asking its
owner to delete it is avoidable merge work, and a sunset note is not a substitute
for not adding the thing. The block is removed rather than retained with an
instruction attached.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-06T15:48:35Z

## DemoB's native lifecycle has left the host — and the cut has an e2e tail nobody has claimed

`b923cb497c` on `agent/18314-demob-native-port` deletes the last consumer copy of the accepted state. `tearOutPanes`, `tearOutConnects` and `tearOutRetirements` are gone from `DemoBWorkspace`, not forwarded — admission, the connect/terminal race, ownership and retirement now read and write through the Group's vessel source, the way `dock/Workspace` and `apps/workstation` already do.

```
$ grep -rn "tearOutPanes\s*=\|tearOutConnects\s*=\|tearOutRetirements\s*=" src apps examples
(no matches)
```

`unit 3431/3431`, 2 skipped. DemoB's own 62 arms pass, and the witness moved with the state: the spec asserts on the Group's admission, connection, ownership and pending retirements.

Two things needed carrying rather than reimplementing, and both are behaviour a rewrite would have dropped:

- **`bound` merges the connection into ownership.** A terminal that beats its connect records ownership before any window exists, so the record names none — and a later disconnect cannot then recognise the generation that died.
- **Retirement stamps the exact native route.** A vessel identity is minted at acquisition, before any window connected; a refused admission surrenders the window it was binding; and the Group re-presents that same identity on every retry. A route not captured at retirement is one no retry can rediscover, and the close degrades silently to closing by name.

## The tail — one defect class, both consumers

The e2e arms still observe these members **as component properties**, and no observation surface replaced them:

| file | sites |
|---|---|
| `e2e/dashboard/TearOutMatrixRows4To7NL` | 19 |
| `e2e/dashboard/DemoBDockTearOutNL` | 6 |
| `e2e/dashboard/DemoBPerspectivesNL` | 4 |
| `e2e/dashboard/DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` | 2 |
| `e2e/dashboard/DemoBVesselConversionNL` | 2 |
| `e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL` | 6 |
| `e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL` | 5 |
| `e2e/workstation/WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` | 5 |
